articles.summary: Bagdad Unveils Flag-Themed Haul Truck Beds mboyle Mon, 07/20/2026 - 08:55 Post Image July 20, 2026 - At the company’s site in Bagdad, Arizona, a new generation of haul truck beds is rolling into service, bringing a wide range of operational benefits – and a timely nod to the country the site helps power. Just ahead of the Fourth of July and America’s 250th anniversary, Bagdad began deploying new Schlam haul truck beds featuring a full American flag design. The first of these beds marks the transition from validation trials to full-scale implementation, as the site continues improvements to its autonomous haulage fleet. “At our operations, every ton matters,” said Nura Woolley, Senior Mine Engineer-FM Technical Services. “This first post-trial bed represents the shift from validation to implementation, driving safer and more efficient performance across the fleet.” Schlam haul truck beds are lighter and more durable than traditional designs, allowing trucks to carry larger payloads, reduce maintenance, shorten dump-cycle times and improve the efficiency of autonomous haulage operations. Bagdad currently targets a 260-ton payload for autonomous, and the new Schlam beds provide roughly four additional tons of capacity. Still, Woolley said the need to support Bagdad’s transition to autonomous haulage was the primary reason for adopting the alternative design there. Bagdad is the first to receive the new painted beds, with 17 units planned for the operation’s initial rollout. Additional deployment is planned across Freeport’s North America sites. Morenci is scheduled to receive 15 beds featuring a variation that incorporates both the U.S. and Arizona state flag, with bed designs for the company’s Colorado and New Mexico operations also in development. While the safety and production benefits drove the decision, the timing of the rollout shaped how the beds would look. With deliveries beginning in the lead-up to the America 250 celebrations, the site saw an opportunity to pair a major equipment upgrade with a visible tribute, said Benny Corbell , Mine Manager-Bagdad. “Make no mistake, these beds are about improving how we operate,” Corbell said. “They’re safer, more efficient and better for the long-term, but the timing made it clear which way we had to go. The people here have a lot of pride in the work they do and the country they do it for, so every time those trucks run, they’ll carry both with them.” Photo: The new haul truck beds being deployed at Bagdad provide several benefits, including increased payload capacity and reduced maintenance requirements.
articles.title: Bagdad Unveils Flag-Themed Haul Truck Beds

articles.summary: Cerro Verde Completes First Works for Taxes Projects in Arequipa mboyle Fri, 07/24/2026 - 09:00 Post Image July 24, 2026 - Cerro Verde has completed its first two projects through Peru's Works for Taxes (Obras por Impuestos, OxI) program, investing more than $14 million in initiatives designed to expand access to education and improve infrastructure in the Arequipa region. The Works for Taxes program allows private companies to accelerate public infrastructure projects by funding and executing them directly, with investments later applied toward tax obligations. Through the program, Cerro Verde is helping ensure a portion of the taxes it pays to the government is translated into tangible improvements for local communities. “The main challenge facing Arequipa’s authorities is improving public investment by spending the resources generated by mining more efficiently—for example, on projects that improve the quality of life of Arequipa residents,” said Julia Torreblanca, Senior Vice President, Corporate Affairs-Cerro Verde. One of the completed projects is a new campus for the National University of San Agustín in El Pedregal, Majes. Developed in partnership with other private companies, the campus includes technology-enabled classrooms, specialized laboratories and research facilities designed to support student learning and innovation. The project is expected to benefit approximately 500 students pursuing degrees in fields such as agronomy and business administration. Cerro Verde also completed a major road infrastructure project in the district of Uchumayo. The work included roadway resurfacing, drainage improvements, signage upgrades, new sidewalks and green spaces. The improvements are expected to enhance traffic flow, increase road safety and support economic development in an important transportation corridor. Both projects generated local employment and reflect Cerro Verde's ongoing commitment to supporting sustainable development in Arequipa. "We do not just extract resources from the earth; we also create opportunities," said Tomás Gonzales, President-Cerro Verde. "When we transform taxes into education and infrastructure, we are building the most valuable legacy we can leave behind: a better future for our people." “Following the successful completion of its first two projects, Cerro Verde currently has eight additional Works for Taxes projects under development that are expected to be completed in the coming months”, said Enrique Aguilar, Social Planning Manager-Cerro Verde. Photos: The new campus for the National University of San Agustín in El Pedregal, Majes, contains well-equipped classroom, laboratories, a library and research space. In the photo above, the road infrastructure projected included roadway resurfacing, drainage improvements, signage upgrades, new sidewalks and green spaces.
articles.title: Cerro Verde Completes First Works for Taxes Projects in Arequipa

articles.summary: Vicki Seppala Retires After Three Decades with Freeport mboyle Thu, 07/16/2026 - 13:48 Post Image July 16, 2026 - Email was the hot new technology when Vicki Seppala first got into the mining business more than three decades ago. Seppala had been working at a technology startup before joining Freeport, so she knew email – like any emerging technology – would create both opportunities and challenges. Email allowed instant and widespread communication. It also gobbled up a lot of time. That lesson stayed with her throughout her career. As a trailblazer who became the first woman mine manager in Chile, Seppala learned that progress often brings both benefits and challenges. Whether evaluating new technologies, managing complex projects or planning for future growth, those experiences proved valuable as she and her team worked to plan the future expansion of the Safford mine and its vast Lone Star reserves. Seppala retired recently as General Manager at Safford, closing a mining career that began in 1995 and took her from an entry-level geological engineer to leadership roles at mine sites across North and South America. Designing the future at Safford As Seppala’s retirement at the end of June neared, her focus was less on herself and more on industry advancements and the outlook for the site where she spent the previous four years. Safford is Freeport’s newest mine in the United States and has the potential to become one of its top producers, with estimates that future expansions could deliver an additional 300 to 400 million pounds of copper per year by the 2030s. It could be in operation for 100 years or more, Seppala said. Helping plan a project of that magnitude and length means predicting what mining will look like decades from now and integrating emerging technology still being developed. It also means working closely with a vast team of technical experts that Seppala credits with “doing the heavy lifting.” The mining industry in general and Freeport in particular have embraced high-tech solutions to squeeze more copper and other metals from the same ore bodies. Like email, that creates new opportunities and challenges. “Trying to understand how to take advantage of the technology that we have when it’s changing so rapidly complicates things a bit,” Seppala said. “It’s exciting and exhilarating to think about how different the Safford mine might look because we have the opportunity to really try to understand the direction that all of these technologies are going and build Safford in a way that can more readily take advantage of those things. It’s liberating because there are so many possibilities. But it’s also very difficult to draw the line in the sand.” Connections to the community Outside of work, Seppala, who graduated from the University of Arizona with a bachelor’s degree in Geological Engineering, has enjoyed time with family and participating in various outdoor activities – hiking, bicycling, camping and wildlife. She also has been active in various civic organizations, including the Lowell Institute for Mineral Resources at the University of Arizona; the Society for Mining, Metallurgy & Exploration; and Women in Mining, where she has served as an advocate and mentor for women pursuing mining careers. “We all live in these communities in which we work,” she said. “We all want to be proud of what we do and make sure that we do what’s right.” One of Seppala’s career highlights is being part of an industry shift that has seen women become a much larger share of the workforce at all levels. A trailblazer herself, Seppala became Chile’s first woman mine manager in 2006 and later served as mine manager at Morenci and general manager of the Climax and Safford mines. Retiring now comes with mixed emotions as this is such a historic time for mining, Seppala said shortly before her last day at Freeport at the end of June. “We are in the middle of writing a very exciting chapter about the dynamic change of mining right now,” she said. “People are going to write books about it in the future, and our company is at the forefront of the innovations in copper processing. It’s going to explode into something that’s game changing in the industry.” Photo: Vicki Seppala was the first woman mine manager in Chile in 2006 and has held other top management positions with Freeport.
articles.title: Vicki Seppala Retires After Three Decades with Freeport

articles.summary: Freeport Ranked One of the Best Companies to Work For in U.S. mboyle Wed, 07/01/2026 - 07:28 Post Image July 1, 2026 - Freeport has been named one the best places to work in the United States in the U.S. News & World Report 2026 Best Companies to Work For ratings. Freeport earned awards in multiple categories – Best Companies to Work For Overall, in the Energy and Resources sector, in the Western U.S. and for Internships. Last year, the company was ranked among the top performers in the Internships category. Employee perceptions of six factors important to their wellbeing are rated. Freeport received top marks in the areas of job and company stability, career opportunities and professional development. It also ranked high on maintaining a work-life balance, creating a sense of belongingness and esteem, quality of pay and benefits, and physical and psychological comfort and safety. The company takes a holistic approach to the employee experience, grounded in Proudly Creating Better Futures—a framework that reflects the value Freeport brings to employees, communities and the world—said Pam Masson, Senior Vice President and Chief Human Resources Officer. This includes investing in career development and skills training, fostering a culture of inclusion and respect, and providing flexibility where possible to support employees both at work and at home. “Being recognized by U.S. News as a Best Company to Work For reflects our commitment to Proudly Creating Better Futures—for our employees, our communities and our business,” Masson said. “We focus on providing competitive pay and benefits, supporting work-life balance, and offering meaningful opportunities for growth—because when our employees succeed, our business does as well.” The publication’s rankings are based on an analysis of about 5,000 of the largest publicly traded and privately held companies in the U.S. To qualify for inclusion on the U.S. News list, a company must score well above the national average for the category, whether it be nationally, in a region or within an industry. Up to 25 percent of top companies in their industry and region are ultimately coined "best," according to the announcement. Employers are evaluated based on publicly available information like company websites, employee reviews on platforms like Glassdoor and LinkedIn, court records, financial strength and governance. Surveys were also conducted to identify the most important factors to employees.
articles.title: Freeport Ranked One of the Best Companies to Work For in U.S.

articles.summary: Manyar Smelter Achieves Copper Mark Designation mboyle Mon, 07/27/2026 - 10:53 Post Image July 27, 2026 - PT Freeport Indonesia’s new smelter in Manyar has attained the Copper Mark after demonstrating it meets global industry standards for protecting workers, the environment and affected communities. With inclusion of the Manyar smelter, all Freeport operating sites have received the Copper Mark or its equivalent for molybdenum. The milestone culminates a seven-month process, with the site being notified in June it had met the requirements. The designation covers the entire Manyar site, including metal refineries and other related facilities. To earn the designation, the facility’s policies and practices were scrutinized by outside auditors to determine whether they complied with rigorous standards that address risk management, business integrity and responsible production. Beyond reviewing written policies, systems and site records, independent auditors spent a week on site in February interviewing management, employees, contractors and community representatives to validate conformance. Demonstrating commitment “The Copper Mark demonstrates PTFI's commitment to the responsible production framework,” said H-D Garz, Executive Vice President-Corporate Planning and Business Strategy at PTFI. “This is not just a ‘tick the box’ exercise. Copper Mark certification elevates our finished goods from both the copper electro refinery and precious metal refinery to products of choice when comparing to other similar products on the market. “Our commitment to operating a massive industrial complex and domestically producing finished products in Gresik in a responsible manner enables us to do this in the most environmentally and socially responsible manner to benefit all stakeholders including the local community.” The Copper Mark was launched in 2019 as a voluntary industry assurance standard that promotes responsible copper production. It is based on 33 criteria that cover a range of categories involving environmental, social and governance performance. Specific policies are required in areas such as labor practices, land and water stewardship, anti-corruption safeguards, biodiversity protection and greenhouse gas emission reductions. The Copper Mark standards are aimed at promoting best practices across the value chain, from mine to market; and minimizing risk, whether it be legal, financial or reputational, said Andrea Boltz, Manager-Responsible Production and Sustainability Assurance. Many customers, including automobile manufacturers and copper wire producers, are requesting the companies that supply them with copper obtain the Copper Mark, Boltz said. Meeting the standards for the Copper Mark also helps enable Freeport to comply with separate but similar responsible copper production requirements to maintain approval on the London Metal Exchange. Key to company strategy “The Copper and Molybdenum Mark are a core component of Freeport’s strategy to demonstrate business value to our shareholders, customers and stakeholders globally regarding sustainability related risks,” said Andrea Vaccari, Vice President-Responsible Production and Sustainability. Copper Mark certification is received by site. While Freeport’s other sites, including the PTFI Grasberg mine in Indonesia, already have the designation, the Manyar smelter was required to demonstrate compliance separately as the company’s newest facility. The process of preparing to seek the Copper Mark began while the smelter was still in the planning stages, said Emily Muteb, Manager-Environmental and Sustainable Development. Corporate policies such as Freeport’s Principles of Business Conduct were foundational, as were Indonesia-specific standards in place at Grasberg. Additional site-specific procedures also were written and documented for the smelter. The early planning proved beneficial as site policies were developed with the Copper Mark standards in mind, Muteb said. “We got to integrate everything from the start,” Muteb said. “We already knew what the rule book was so we could build our business processes around it, instead of looking at the rule book and having to change our business processes.” Operations at the Manyar smelter were curtailed in a state of “hot preservation” after a fatal mudslide at the Grasberg Block Cave in 2025 and it has operated on a limited basis since. It is planned to resume full operations later this year. The separate smelter in nearby Gresik is not included in the Copper Mark designation. Freeport is part of the consortium, PT Smelting, that operates the smelter. However, it is not the operating partner. Photos (top to bottom): A worker conducts matte tapping at the Manyar smelter in Indonesia before it was put in a state of “hot preservation” with curtailed operations last year. The smelter is planned to resume full operations later this year; the integrated cooling system, which protects the smelter furnace, is checked during a recent maintenance inspection at the Manyar smelter.
articles.title: Manyar Smelter Achieves Copper Mark Designation

articles.summary: Fellowship Offers College Professors Real-World Experience mboyle Fri, 07/31/2026 - 11:14 Post Image July 31, 2026 - Years of academia recently made way for months of invaluable, real-world experience for 12 college professors participating in Freeport’s Academic-Industry Mining (AIM) Fellowship. Through the AIM Fellowship, college professors from across the country temporarily trade academia for summer work experience, gaining an in-depth, hands-on understanding of the mining process and the challenges it faces. For Azeem Raza, the fellowship not only represents an opportunity to understand the current landscape of the mining industry but also help shape it, literally. Raza, an assistant research professor at Missouri University of Science and Technology, specializes in surface mine design and planning. He is spending his fellowship with Freeport’s Reinvent Mining team, exploring how emerging technologies like autonomous haulage and robotics could fundamentally change the way mines are designed and operated. “Mine planning has traditionally been built around people,” Raza said. “Traffic patterns, facility placement, haul road distances, all of them are optimized for humans and human-operated equipment. The rise of autonomous systems is creating entirely new possibilities for how future mines could be designed and operated, requiring new skill sets for mining engineers.” Working with the Reinvent Mining team, Raza hopes to bring that insight back into the classroom, helping prepare a generation of engineers beginning their education as these new technologies are being introduced. Kate Brown Requist, an assistant professor of mining engineering at the University of Tennessee, also plans to use her fellowship experience in the classroom. Brown Requist comes from a family steeped in service and mining. Inspired by a first responder parent and a sibling working in the mining industry, Brown Requist found a way to combine those influences through a career focused on mine safety. During the fellowship, Brown Requist has been examining underground mine ventilation systems, including those used at PT Freeport Indonesia, to better understand the practical considerations that go into maintaining safe and effective work environments. The AIM Fellowship, which started in 2017 and was temporarily suspended during the COVID-19 pandemic, restarted last year and has grown this year with the placement of 12 fellows. As mining continues to evolve, it is more important than ever for Freeport to support those preparing the next generation of mining professionals, said Angie Harmon, Regional Manager of Social Performance-North America. The fellowship gives educators firsthand exposure to the industry, which in turn helps students better understand the range of careers available to them. “One of our biggest challenges is perception,” Harmon said. “By engaging educators like this, we’re creating opportunities for their students to see just how much has changed and better appreciate some very real employment possibilities. We’re creating a pipeline to our future workforce.” For Brown Requist, that direct exposure helps bridge the gap between academic instruction and industry practice. “In academia, it can be easy to get locked in the ivory tower,” Brown Requist said. “Programs like the AIM Fellowship give educators real-world knowledge about the modern mining industry, helping students better understand its realities and needs in a way that will prepare them to make a difference.” Photo (top to bottom): Through the fellowship, Kate Brown Requist (left) and Azeem Raza look to bring firsthand experience into the classroom; This year, 12 AIM fellows joined various company initiatives, toured operations and more to better understand modern mining.
articles.title: Fellowship Offers College Professors Real-World Experience

articles.summary: GRESIK MINE LOCATED IN PAPUA, INDONESIA mboyle Thu, 07/23/2026 - 13:36 Operation Region INDONESIA Ores Copper and Gold Ores Location Display Order 2 Modal Background Image Map Location id #gresik_link Left Column • PTFI’s Smelter and Precious Metals Refinery • PT Smelting (Copper Smelter and Refinery) Description PTFI’s smelter at Manyar, Gresik, East Java, and the nearby PT Smelting operation smelt and refine all of the copper concentrate from PTFI, and the Precious Metals Refinery at the Manyar smelter processes anode slimes from the smelter and PT Smelting. Did you know? With the completion of PTFI’s smelter and precious metals refinery (PMR) (collectively, PTFI’s downstream processing facilities) in Gresik, Indonesia, during 2025, PTFI is a fully integrated producer of refined copper and gold. Location Gresik is a city and regency located in East Java Province, Indonesia, on the island of Java. Gresik is approximately 650 kilometers east of Jakarta. Background During 2024, construction of PTFI’s smelter in Eastern Java, Indonesia, was completed. In October 2024, during start-up activities, a fire occurred that required a temporary suspension of smelting operations to complete repairs. Operations commenced in May 2025 following completion of repairs, and in July 2025, PTFI’s smelter produced its first copper cathode. Following the September 2025 mud rush incident, smelting operations in Indonesia at both PTFI’s smelter and PT Smelting were adjusted as a result of limited copper concentrate availability. In late December 2025, PT Smelting resumed operations. Shipments to PTFI’s smelter are expected to recommence in the second half of 2026 at a reduced rate dependent on available copper concentrate from mining operations at the Grasberg Block Cave underground mine. The PMR has operated on a limited basis since the September 2025 mud rush incident, primarily processing anode slimes from PT Smelting. PT Smelting is an Indonesia company that owns a copper smelter and refinery in Gresik, Indonesia. In 1996, PTFI entered into a joint venture and shareholder agreement with Mitsubishi Materials Corporation to jointly construct the PT Smelting facilities. PT Smelting commenced operations in 1999. In December 2023, PT Smelting completed the expansion of its capacity by 30% to process approximately 1.3 million metric tons of copper concentrate per year. Right Column Smelter Capacity PTFI’s Manyar smelter has a capacity to process approximately 1.7 million metric tons of copper concentrate per year. In 2025, copper anode production from PTFI’s smelter totaled 54,100 metric tons and copper cathode production from its refinery totaled 42,600 metric tons. As part of start-up activities, PTFI commenced gold production from the PMR in December 2024 and operated on a limited basis during 2025, primarily processing anode slimes from PT Smelting. The PMR has a design capacity to refine anode slimes from PTFI’s smelter as well as from PT Smelting. Anode slimes processed through the PMR totaled 1,900 metric tons in 2025. PT Smelting has a capacity to process approximately 1.3 million metric tons of copper concentrate per year. Ownership 48.76% of PTFI is owned by FCX; 51.24% share ownership is collectively held by PT Mineral Industri Indonesia (MIND ID), an Indonesia state-owned enterprise, and PT Indonesia Papua Metal Dan Mineral (formerly known as PT Indocopper Investama), which is expected to be owned by MIND ID and the provincial/regional government in Central Papua, Indonesia. PT Smelting is PTFI’s 66%-owned smelter and refinery in Gresik, Indonesia. Mitsubishi Materials Corporation owns the remaining 34% of PT Smelting’s outstanding common stock and serves as the operator of the facilities. articles.summary: Bagdad Hosts Corporate Interns for Annual Site Visit mboyle Fri, 07/10/2026 - 13:40 Post Image July 10, 2026- The company’s corporate interns recently traded the quiet hum of the office for the din of a fully producing mine, traveling to Bagdad for a tour that connected their work with day-to-day site operations. The tour was part of the “Intern Extravaganza,” a yearly event arranged for the summer interns by Freeport’s Talent Acquisition Programs team. Nearly 40 interns participated in this year’s Bagdad tour. In total, the company has close to 200 interns this summer, a mix of office and in-the-field workers experiencing modern mining across various Freeport sites and specialties. After last year’s visit to Sierrita, the Phoenix-based interns’ tour of Bagdad has returned as an annual part of the Extravaganza. In addition to getting a firsthand look at a mining operation, the interns also learned more about Bagdad’s initiatives, including the planned Bagdad 2X expansion, the Sycamore Tailings Storage Facility beginning construction and, of course, the Bagdad autonomous haulage system. While in Bagdad, the corporate interns toured key areas of the operation, including the mine shop, SX plant, tailings, mill concentrator and concentrate leach plant. At each stage of the tour, site leaders and subject matter experts were on hand to explain the role each area plays in the site’s broader operations. The tour closed out with a visit to the mine overlook, where the interns could watch the autonomous haul trucks in action, before getting a behind-the-scenes look in the command center. “We had a really great time on site,” said Isabella Cutaia, Temporary Summer Intern-Global Supply Chain. “We saw the autonomous trucks from the upper level and control room side. I think being able to transfer everything that we’ve seen at site and what we see on our systems working from the corporate office is really helpful.” Beyond the Bagdad visit, the two-day Intern Extravaganza also included an afternoon at the company’s Phoenix Hub, where interns took part in team-building exercises, networking opportunities and heard from former interns who transitioned to full-time roles with Freeport. Alyssa Kohn, Talent Acquisition Supervisor, said the two-day event plays an important role in helping interns understand the company’s operations, connect their work to broader organizational goals and build relationships that support future career opportunities. “The extravaganza is a chance for our interns to connect and develop professionally, as well as see how different parts of the business come together,” Kohn said. “The Talent Acquisition Programs team understands how important that is and puts a great deal of effort into planning the Hub programming and site visit. It’s an opportunity to create a connected experience that helps interns see how their roles – and their goals – fit within the company.” Photo (top to bottom): Interns Isabella Cutaia (left) and Samahara Quintana Chavez take in the sights at Bagdad’s new command center; Corporate interns receive an up-close look at one of Bagdad’s autonomous haul trucks.
articles.title: Bagdad Hosts Corporate Interns for Annual Site Visit
